Tessa / Rachel —

Thanks for the MAP draft you sent yesterday. Alicia and I ran it by procurement and legal this morning; a few rapid questions so we can commit to the proposed sprint windows:

- We need clarity on the "binding" milestone that triggers invoicing for the order form. Can Redwood accept an order-form-signature-first flow while MSA redlines are finalized (procurement prefers to avoid delaying pilots)?
- DPA: Helix requires confirmation on data residency and subprocessor list before a final execution. How long to obtain the latest SOC2/HIPAA evidence artifacts?
- Acceptance gates: the MAP lists a 10-business-day acceptance window. Our technical lead asked whether that can be reduced to 5 business days with a short-list of acceptance tests.

We're trying to accelerate to a pilot start on 2027-05-03. Is that realistic if legal redlines start today?

Appreciate a quick cadence on owners and hard blockers.

—Mark

Mark / Alicia —

Thanks — we can support an accelerated, conditional-signature path but we need to align on three controlled workstreams and owners so nothing slips:

1) Legal & Redlines (owner: karthik_iyer) — target: 3 business days for initial pass on standard commercial redlines; escalate any SOW/indemnity/DPA items that need Exec review.
2) Security & Evidence (owner: rachel_kim) — we'll pull SOC2 report and the subprocessor list today, expect delivery by EOD tomorrow (2027-04-20).
3) Acceptance & Pilot Runbook (owner: vanessa_ortiz) — narrow acceptance to 5 business days if Helix provides a reduced test matrix (we can support automated smoke tests).

Proposed conditional flow we recommend:
- Day 0 (today): Order form signed as "binding for pilot" with explicit clause: "Order form effectiveness contingent on MSA execution within 15 business days OR escrow of contested provisions".
- Legal works redlines in parallel; if redlines are material, charter an Exec sign-off window (48 hrs).
- Security artifacts delivered prior to pilot kickoff.

I'll attach a MAP with rows for each milestone and dependency (Helix_MAP_v3.xlsx) and our suggested language for the conditional order-form clause. Can Helix confirm owners for the reduced acceptance matrix today so Vanessa can lock test cases?

If all three streams hit their targets, 2027-05-03 pilot start is achievable. If legal extends beyond 10 business days we recommend a short-term credit holdback instead of postponing the pilot.

Thanks — looping in owners to keep momentum.

—Tessa Morgan

Mark / Team —

Thanks for surfacing. Quick procurement/legal sequencing proposal from our side to keep the pilot date:

Step 1 — Initial redline pass (owner: karthik_iyer) — 3 business days. I will triage the Draft_MSA_redlines_20270418.docx today and return a marked-up file.

Step 2 — DPA confirmation & evidence (owner: rachel_kim) — SOC2 report + subprocessor list delivered by 2027-04-20 EOD. If Helix requires additional certifications, flag them now.

Step 3 — Conditional order form signature (owner: tessa_morgan) — sign OrderForm_Appendix_A.pdf today with the conditional effectiveness clause (sample language below). This enables pilot invoicing while legal finishes: 
- "Order Form becomes effective upon signature for the pilot only. Final commercial effectiveness of the Order Form is subject to execution of the MSA within 15 business days of Order Form signature. In the event the MSA is not executed within 15 business days, the parties agree to enter a governance process and either (a) finalize outstanding terms within 5 business days, or (b) execute a one-time credit holdback not to exceed 15% of the pilot MRC."

Step 4 — Acceptance & go/no-go (owner: vanessa_ortiz) — run the 5 prioritized tests during the 5-business-day acceptance window. If Helix signs-off, convert pilot to production provisioning.

If we start this cadence today, target pilot kickoff 2027-05-03 remains feasible. If any party requests extended legal review beyond 10 business days, we should adopt the credit holdback (or escrow) to keep timeline intact.

I'll queue the redline deliverable by EOD and stand by for Helix's 5-case acceptance matrix.

—Karthik Iyer
Director, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
